## [2026-10-26](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-26.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [KnitTrans: Coordinated Trajectory Transfer for Effective and Efficient LLM Reinforcement Learning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32389>)

KnitTrans admits rollout trajectories in smaller batches while reserving enough capacity to satisfy final training quotas, then aligns data transfer with each training consumer. It also reuses multimodal encodings while aggregating their gradients correctly, reducing pipeline-induced data staleness and repeated transfer without abandoning the specified batch constraints.

**Published:** 2026-10-23 · **First seen:** 2026-10-26T10:03:21.065Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** RL Pipelines, Trajectory Transfer, Batch Constraints, Multimodal Training

**Public availability:** 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.DC/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32389v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full 14-page v1 inspected. Atomic storage units, micro-batch prefetch and gradient-preserving encoder dedup complement quota-feasibility guards. Tests use 256 Hopper GPUs, three large models, FP8 training/inference and disaggregated GRPO. Authors report up to 93% lower additional parameter-version gap versus train-batch admission, and up to 5.8× faster transfer plus training on multimodal workloads. Receipt: October 23 09:15UTC; the original October 26 cs.DC batch and official Sunday schedule imply October 26 00:00UTC announcement. Earlier TransferQueue/slime are background; no KnitTrans code destination was verified.

**Limitations:** The 5.8× excludes rollout time and depends on the tested multimodal reuse. Staleness measures extra version age versus colocated execution, not all policy lag. Quality evidence is a short MiMo reward curve, not final multi-seed convergence. Private grounding datasets, unspecified Hopper SKU and application-specific quota assumptions limit generalization.

## [2026-10-16](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-16.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [ReFlow: Replay-Driven Decoupling for Efficient RL Post-Training](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21640>)

ReFlow mixes a bounded, down-weighted share of recently used trajectories into asynchronous reinforcement-learning batches, reducing the trainer's dependence on expensive fresh rollouts. Prewarmed workers and an adaptive scheduler move GPUs between generation and training as demand changes, increasing processed-training-token throughput while preserving comparable training-reward progress in the tested reasoning and agent workloads.

**Published:** 2026-10-15 · **First seen:** 2026-10-17T10:02:23.384Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Experience Replay, Asynchronous RL, Elastic Workers, Rollout Scheduling

**Public availability:** 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21640>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Reviewed Sections 1-8, the replay-weighting analysis, worker transitions, both schedulers and complete evaluations. The VeRL/Ray/vLLM/FSDP2 system tests Qwen3-4B/8B/14B/32B on 8-128 H800 GPUs using DAPO math, APPS coding and ReTool sandbox reasoning. Replay fraction and replay loss weight are capped/set at 0.5, with maximum policy lag one; sampling is random and reinsertion unfiltered. Authors report up to 2.06x trainer-processed token throughput, reward-versus-step/time curves, and 5.72/9.20 s resource rebalances on 32 GPUs. Public-paper timing is inferred from the PRIMARY cs.LG October 16 batch and official release schedule, rather than the October 15 receipt timestamp.

**Limitations:** Throughput includes replayed tokens consumed by the trainer; it is not fresh-trajectory generation throughput. Quality evidence is training reward rather than held-out reasoning or coding evaluation. Throughput windows are five measured steps after five warmups, or ten after ten for coding. The local gradient-error argument assumes unbiased unused samples, bounded replay bias and uncorrelated centered errors; it is not a global convergence guarantee. Prewarmed hybrid workers require CPU offload and compatible replica groups, and adaptation depends on workload. The code is awaiting approval and not yet released. No independent reproduction was performed.

## [2026-10-15](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-15.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Finish RL Training Faster: Bitwise-Consistent, High-Performance, Agent-Driven](<https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-14-train-inference-consistency>)

This engineering report makes training recomputation and vLLM rollout share a numerical execution path, aligning low-precision kernels, routing and reduction order so sampled-token probabilities match bit for bit in the tested recipes. It documents DeepSeek and Mamba-hybrid transfers plus an agent-assisted debugging workflow, providing a practical recipe for reducing train-rollout mismatch while making the remaining throughput and training-quality trade-offs explicit.

**Published:** 2026-10-14 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T15:09:52.031Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Train-Rollout Consistency, Low Precision, Agentic RL, vLLM

**Public availability:** 2026-10-14T09:00:00Z (dated primary source). [Timing source](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm-project.github.io/main/_posts/2026-10-14-train-inference-consistency.md>)

[Blog](<https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-14-train-inference-consistency>) · [Code](<https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7688>) · [Project](<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61551>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. Delayed discovery: blog front matter documents Oct 14 09:00 UTC, one hour before this daily window but within 72 h. Complete blog/technical tables and linked preview PR descriptions inspected. DeepSeek-V4-Flash GRPO uses 32 GB200 GPUs, 128 prompts x 8 responses and one update/step; over 100 steps authors report exactly zero same-weight token differences and 91.3% of baseline rollout throughput. Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B NVFP4 on 8 GB200 nodes retains training reward on a 375-task filtered SWE-bench Pro training subset. The contribution covered is the detailed dated report and transfer evidence; existing DeepSeek preview PR opened Sep 2, and bitwise consistency is not a new invention here.

**Limitations:** No end-to-end wall-clock gain was measured; training overhead was not separately isolated. The 91.3% rollout ratio includes differing response lengths and late baseline degradation; first 89 steps give 88.6%. Each baseline has one untuned recipe without TIS/MIS; collapse is not universal. Same-weight forward equality does not prove gradient correctness or account for stale/asynchronously changed policies. Recipe requires one update/step and TP=1; speculative decoding is not covered. Code links are preview/open PRs, not an asserted upstream release. No independent reproduction.

## [2026-10-14](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-14.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Prorsa: Unleashing the Potential of Prefill-Decode Disaggregation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16592>)

Prorsa monitors agent trajectories, sandbox startup and tool execution to forecast short-term prefill and decode demand, then switches rollout workers between the two roles. This adapts disaggregated inference to multi-turn reinforcement learning, reducing interference and cache-capacity bottlenecks; the authors report 1.11–4.05x faster agentic rollouts, with slowdowns in most tested single-turn math settings.

**Published:** 2026-10-12 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:36:43.360Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Agentic RL, Prefill Decode Disaggregation, Workload Prediction

**Public availability:** 2026-10-14T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.DC/recent>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16592>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–5 inspect workload characterization, lifecycle prediction and adaptive allocation atop Verl/SGLang. Experiments use FP8 Qwen3-235B-A22B, DeepSeek-V3.2 and MiMo-V2.5-Pro on a 16-server, 128-GPU cluster with NVLink and 400-Gbps RDMA NICs, comparing rollout time against prefill-decode colocation. Role switching adds 1.0–1.44x over task-tuned static splits in the MiMo ablation. The October 12 v1 submission predates its verified October 14 announcement batch.

**Limitations:** Rollout speedups do not measure full training time or final policy quality. Results depend strongly on attention parallelism and task mix; KV transfer and switching can hurt single-turn workloads. Decode allocation forecasts admission-cache volume without explicitly predicting output lengths or near-term cache reclamation. GPU model and a dedicated code release were not verified.

### [NeMo-DCR: Bit-Exact Delta-Compressed Refit for Scalable Agentic RL at Trillion-Parameter Scale](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08430>)

The NeMo-DCR paper evaluates sparse synchronization of changed weight bits between training and rollout systems with different shard layouts. Canonical coordinates, selective conversion and retry-safe repairs reduce transfer volume while preserving exact dense-refit results under stated loader and failure assumptions.

**Published:** 2026-10-06 · **First seen:** 2026-10-07T10:05:15Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Weight Synchronization, Agentic RL, Delta Compression, Failure Recovery

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 8.1–8.6 evaluate cross-region refits with 32 GB300 training GPUs and 64 H100 rollout GPUs. At 3% synthetic changes, Table 4 reports 22.6 seconds for 120B relay refit versus 750 seconds for full-checkpoint transport. Separate 30B GRPO experiments span 50 steps and five runs, including injected receiver failures.

**Limitations:** The reference measures transport only, not dense load or end-to-end RL. Stress tests use synthetic 3–5% changes; 1T doubles Nemotron-550B layers. Exactness is conditional; quantized rollout is unsupported. This is a new paper/evaluation of code merged in July, not a new implementation release. No results were reproduced. The linked PR's still-open recovery issue describes checkpoint reload after partial failure; parity with the paper's transactional recovery protocol was not independently verified.

## [2026-10-05](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-05.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [VenusRL: A Fully Disaggregated Agentic RL System with Priority Scheduling and Scalable Interaction](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03286>)

VenusRL separates training, generation, and tool execution, then prioritizes rollout groups that can unblock the next policy update while protecting their cached state. Coordinating generation priorities with sandbox admission and shared memory reduces wasted work and environment memory pressure in long, multi-turn reinforcement learning.

**Published:** 2026-10-02 · **First seen:** 2026-10-05T10:03:36Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Agentic RL, Rollout Scheduling, KV Residency, Sandbox Memory

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03286>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Original v1 was submitted October 2 at 13:29:40 UTC; the October 5 announcement list and official schedule place public release at October 5 00:00 UTC, inside the main window. The older submission date is retained with the legacy newly-discovered label. Sections 6.1–6.3 evaluate Qwen3-4B/32B OpenSWE training on 32 Hopper GPUs and report 1.06–4.24x end-to-end throughput over RollFlash across tested batch and asynchrony settings, with component ablations.

**Limitations:** Gains depend on batching and asynchrony. The learned length predictor and sandbox sharing depend on workload characteristics; representative convergence plots do not establish universal learning equivalence. The paper identifies Hopper GPUs without specifying the accelerator model. No public VenusRL implementation was verified, and no results were reproduced.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [AReaL: A Large-Scale Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning System for Language Reasoning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24298>)

AReaL separates rollout generation from policy updates so workers can keep producing and consuming training data without waiting for the longest response in a batch. Staleness control and a modified policy objective help retain learning quality while improving GPU utilization, providing an open reference for asynchronous reasoning-model reinforcement learning.

**Published:** 2025-05-30 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Asynchronous RL, Rollouts, Policy Staleness

**Positioning:** open-reference

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24298>) · [Code](<https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The authors evaluate mathematical and code reasoning across 1.5B–32B models and ablate policy staleness and interruptible generation; the original experiments report up to 2.57x throughput versus synchronous configurations.

**Limitations:** The gains depend on balancing generation and training; short generations can reduce the advantage, and excessive policy staleness still harms learning. Results are author-reported and software-version specific.
